key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2-NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this does not translate into better erosion resistance at 90° impact.
engineering_relevance: Axial-feeding HV-APS is a promising route for improving wear performance of cermet coatings on steel components where tribological durability matters most.
method: Cr3C2-NiCr coatings sprayed on S235 steel by APS (radial injection) and HV-APS (axial feeding)
Compared porosity, microhardness, phase composition, erosion behavior, and ball-on-disc wear
Related performance to microstructure and carbide decomposition/solid-solution formation
evidence_signal: HV-APS cut porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, raised hardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and lowered wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3, while erosion rates stayed nearly unchanged at 0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g.
watch_item: The improved density and hardness mainly benefited sliding wear; high-angle erosion showed little difference, so process choice should match the dominant service loading.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
